title: PyVision-RL: Forging Open Agentic Vision Models via RL
one_liner: Train a vision agent to keep using tools across several turns by rewarding useful interaction instead of short direct answers.
lead: This paper studies a failure mode in reinforcement learning for vision agents. During training, the agent often discovers that it can get reward by answering quickly, so it stops using tools and stops carrying out multi-step reasoning. PyVision-RL changes the rollout and reward design so that sustained interaction remains worth doing because useful tool calls keep contributing to the final score.

problem.h2: Why agent training collapses into short answers
paras: A vision agent is supposed to inspect images or video, call tools when needed, and combine evidence across several turns. Standard reinforcement learning can break that behavior. If short replies sometimes get reward, the agent may learn to skip the expensive parts of the job because skipping tools is an easy way to avoid mistakes.

That collapse matters because many image and video tasks need step-by-step evidence gathering. A model that refuses to inspect more frames or refuses to call a helpful tool may look cheaper during training, but it solves fewer tasks because it never collects the information that the task requires.

callout.b: The paper's move in one sentence.
callout.html: Keep multi-turn tool use alive by sampling several candidate rollouts, keeping the useful ones, ranking them, and giving reward for productive tool interaction.

panels.title: 2. A shortcut appears

panels.title: 4. PyVision-RL reshapes the score

panels.caption: The trained agent keeps checking evidence across turns because that behavior now helps its training score.

steps.text: For one task, produce several candidate interaction traces so that training can compare short and long behaviors.
Remove low-quality candidates so that the model is not pushed toward obviously bad behavior.
Order the remaining traces by task quality so that the update favors stronger solutions.
Give extra credit when tool use contributes to solving the task because the agent should not learn that all tool calls are wasted effort.
For video tasks, fetch only the frames needed at the current step so that the agent keeps enough visual evidence without loading the whole clip at once.

paras: The paper changes the training signal for agent behavior. Instead of treating a short correct answer and a carefully gathered answer as almost the same event, it values the interaction trace itself when that trace contains useful evidence gathering.
object.object: the training score over multi-turn interaction traces

hidden.name: whether interaction remains worth doing during training
paras: The central hidden quantity is the model's internal preference for using tools and continuing a search. You cannot read that preference directly. You only see it through choices such as whether the agent asks for more frames, opens a tool, or stops early.

PyVision-RL tries to keep that hidden preference pointed toward productive interaction. It does that by rewarding traces where extra steps genuinely help because the agent should learn that useful evidence gathering is part of the job, not wasted motion.

heat.caption: Darker cells mark actions that the training setup should keep valuable because they often gather or organize needed evidence.

reads.html: The hidden quantity is the agent's willingness to keep working through the task instead of quitting early.
The method tries to preserve sustained interaction by reshaping rollout selection and reward so that useful multi-turn behavior remains part of the best-scoring policy.

mechanism.h2: Why this works: reward the process that finds the evidence
paras: Interaction collapse happens when the training score says that a short reply is good enough often enough. Once that shortcut appears, the agent stops practicing search behavior because the shortcut is easier to repeat than careful evidence gathering.

PyVision-RL changes that pressure in two ways. First, it samples and ranks multiple traces, so the update sees strong interactive traces instead of only one lucky output. Second, it adds explicit reward for useful tool activity, so the model learns that checking images, checking video frames, and continuing the dialogue can raise the score because those actions support the final answer.

math.h2: Score a rollout by answer quality plus useful interaction
math.words: A simple summary is to score each candidate trace by combining how well it solves the task and how much useful tool interaction it contains. Training prefers traces with larger total score.

how well the trace solves the image or video task

worked.title: A tiny worked example
lines: Trace A gives a quick answer with no extra checks.
Its task value is 7 and its tool value is 0, so with lambda = 1 its total score is 7.
Trace B checks two useful frames and then answers correctly.
Its task value is 7 and its tool value is 3, so its total score is 10.
Training prefers Trace B because the extra interaction found useful evidence.

math.note: The paper uses a richer reinforcement-learning setup, but this score captures the main idea that interaction must stay rewarding when it contributes to the answer.

items.html: If the score rewards tool calls too loosely, the agent may call tools without learning from them, because empty interaction can still collect points.

items.b: Filtering can drop unusual good traces.
items.html: A useful trace may look weak at first glance and get removed, so the model can lose a path that would have taught a better strategy because the ranking signal was noisy early on.

items.b: On-demand frame choice can miss late evidence.
items.html: If the video selector fetches the wrong frames, the final answer can fail because the model never saw the decisive moment.
The framework is valuable because it treats agent behavior itself as something that must be protected during training, not only the final answer string.

demo.h2: What a runnable demo should prove
paras: Build one image task set and one video task set where correct answers require extra evidence gathering. Train one agent with plain reinforcement learning and one with the PyVision-RL scoring setup. For the video tasks, let the second agent request frames during reasoning instead of loading the whole clip at the start.

The demo should show that the PyVision-RL agent keeps making tool calls on hard tasks because those calls help recover needed evidence. Track both final accuracy and average number of useful interaction steps so that the result shows quality and behavior together.
demo.metric_eq: interaction_gain = useful_steps_pyvision - useful_steps_baseline ; answer_gain = accuracy_pyvision - accuracy_baseline
demo.closing: The point of the demo is to show that better answers come from keeping evidence-gathering behavior alive during training because the agent keeps collecting the facts needed for hard tasks.
